cues.en: Welcome to the stage, Chris Ermsen, presenting his talk,
cues.zh: 欢迎 Chris Ermsen 登台，带来他的演讲：

cues.en: Google Self-Driving Car Project.
cues.zh: Google 自动驾驶汽车项目。

cues.en: Wow, well, good afternoon, and thanks for coming out
cues.zh: 哇，大家下午好，感谢各位前来

cues.en: to hear the talk.
cues.zh: 听这场演讲。

cues.en: I can tell you, I've given a bunch of talks,
cues.zh: 说实话，我做过很多次演讲，

cues.en: and I've never had President Obama open for me.
cues.zh: 但还从没让奥巴马总统给我开过场。

cues.en: So see what I can do to follow that.
cues.zh: 我看看接下来自己能讲成什么样吧。

cues.en: Today, I'm going to talk to you about the work we've
cues.zh: 今天，我要和大家聊聊我们在 Google

cues.en: been doing at Google on self-driving cars,
cues.zh: 开展的自动驾驶汽车研发工作，

cues.en: a little bit of the history before that, a little bit
cues.zh: 讲一点此前的背景历史，聊聊

cues.en: about why we're doing this work,
cues.zh: 我们为什么要做这件事，

cues.en: and a little about when you can expect
cues.zh: 以及大家大概什么时候能看到

cues.en: to see it on the roads.
cues.zh: 它们真正上路。

cues.en: But before I get started, you know, I have the great privilege of coming here today
cues.zh: 但在开始之前，大家知道，我今天非常荣幸能来到这里

cues.en: to talk to you.
cues.zh: 和大家交流。

cues.en: But really, the work I'm going to show you is that of our incredibly dedicated team we
cues.zh: 但实际上，我要展示的成果都来自 Google 一支极其敬业的团队，

cues.en: have at Google, whose mission is to improve people's lives by transforming mobility.
cues.zh: 他们的使命就是通过变革出行方式，来改善人们的生活。

cues.en: And they come into work every day to push that forward and try and make the world better.
cues.zh: 他们每天来上班都是为了推进这项事业，努力让世界变得更美好。

cues.en: Our story starts 130 years ago when Carl Benz invented the automobile.
cues.zh: 我们的故事始于 130 年前，卡尔·本茨（Carl Benz）发明了汽车。

cues.en: And the first time he took it out in public to showcase his invention, you know what
cues.zh: 而他第一次当众展示他的这项发明时，你们猜

cues.en: he did?
cues.zh: 发生了什么？

cues.en: it, he crashed it into a wall. 60 years ago, the America's power companies put this ad
cues.zh: 他把它撞到了墙上。60年前，美国的电力公司在

cues.en: in A Boy's Life magazine. The idea being that you get in your self-driving car wearing
cues.zh: 《Boy's Life》杂志上刊登了这样一则广告。广告里描绘的场景是：你穿着西装坐进自动驾驶汽车，

cues.en: your suit, playing dominoes with your lovely wife, it would follow buried cables in the
cues.zh: 和可爱的妻子一起玩多米诺骨牌，汽车沿着埋在地下的电缆行驶，

cues.en: ground and take you where you want it to go. So the idea of self-driving cars isn't
cues.zh: 带你去你想去的地方。所以自动驾驶汽车的概念

cues.en: something new. It's just something where in the last few years, we've had the technology
cues.zh: 并不新鲜。只是在过去的几年里，我们才拥有了

cues.en: you to really make some exciting advances.
cues.zh: 能真正取得令人兴奋的突破的技术。

cues.en: But even 20 years ago, we had cars that could drive across the country.
cues.zh: 但即便在20年前，我们就已经有了能横穿全美的汽车。

cues.en: These are colleagues of mine from Carnegie Mellon University, who had a research program
cues.zh: 这是我在 Carnegie Mellon University 的同事们，他们当时有一个研究项目，

cues.en: called No Hands Across America.
cues.zh: 叫做“无人驾驶横穿美国”（No Hands Across America）。

cues.en: And what they did is they took this minivan, outfitted it with a camera and some computers,
cues.zh: 他们的做法是改造了这辆小型面包车，装上了摄像头和一些电脑，

cues.en: and had it drive 98% of the way across the country without touching the steering wheel.
cues.zh: 让它在不触碰方向盘的情况下，横穿全美完成了98%的行程。

cues.en: So exciting times, lots of work over the last many decades has gone into this field,
cues.zh: 那真是令人兴奋的岁月，在过去的几十年里，这个领域倾注了大量的心血，

cues.en: But we haven't yet seen it out in the world.
cues.zh: 但我们尚未在现实世界中真正看到它的普及。

cues.en: For me, the story in this space started in 2003.
cues.zh: 对我而言，在这个领域的故事始于2003年。

cues.en: That was when the Defense Department announced the DARPA Grand Challenge.
cues.zh: 当时美国国防部公布了 DARPA Grand Challenge。

cues.en: The idea here was that we'd have robots drive from Los Angeles to Las Vegas, about 150
cues.zh: 它的设想是让机器人驾驶汽车从洛杉矶开到拉斯维加斯，穿越沙漠，

cues.en: miles across the desert.
cues.zh: 全程大约150英里。

cues.en: You weren't allowed to have remote controls.
cues.zh: 不能使用遥控器。

cues.en: You weren't allowed to wrap a midget in aluminum foil and hide them inside and hope
cues.zh: 也不能把侏儒用铝箔包起来藏在车里，然后祈祷

cues.en: it all worked out.
cues.zh: 一切顺利。

cues.en: It had to be honest to goodness, a car that could drive itself across the desert.
cues.zh: 它必须是一辆货真价实、能自己穿越沙漠的车。

cues.en: So our team of grad students and faculty got together, and we went out to the desert to
cues.zh: 于是我们的研究生和教授组成了团队，一起前往沙漠，

cues.en: see how it would go.
cues.zh: 想看看情况会如何。

cues.en: And you know, it was an adventure.
cues.zh: 你们懂的，这真是一场冒险。

cues.en: This was 10 days before the race.
cues.zh: 当时距离比赛还有十天。

cues.en: Our vehicle went out, tripped over a little bit of soft mud, and smashed into the ground.
cues.zh: 我们的车开了出去，被一小块软泥绊了一下，直接砸在地上。

cues.en: We got the thing put back together because we had an army of graduate students.
cues.zh: 多亏我们有一大批研究生，才把车重新拼装好。

cues.en: We entered in the competition, and that year, it launched out from the starting gate.
cues.zh: 我们参加了比赛，那一年，车子冲出了发车闸门。

cues.en: It drove seven miles, crashed through three or four fence posts, ended up on a berm, basically
cues.zh: 它开了七英里，撞断了三四根栅栏柱，最后停在一道土坡上，基本上

cues.en: on fire.
cues.zh: 起火了。

cues.en: It was thrilling, right?
cues.zh: 太刺激了，对吧？

cues.en: And you can imagine the Defense Department and we were just massacred in the press,
cues.zh: 你可以想象，国防部和我们当时在媒体上被喷得有多惨，

cues.en: right?
cues.zh: 对吧？

cues.en: It was a 150-mile race, and the best competitor went seven miles.
cues.zh: 那是一场150英里的比赛，而成绩最好的选手只跑了7英里。

cues.en: But what was exciting of those 7 miles, we drove some of them at 40 miles per hour, again,
cues.zh: 但令人兴奋的是，在这7英里中，我们有些路段开到了时速40英里，而且，

cues.en: all by itself, no one on board.
cues.zh: 完全是自主驾驶，车上空无一人。

cues.en: And at the time, that was a big deal.
cues.zh: 在当时，这可是一件了不起的大事。

cues.en: And so the Defense Department said, come back next year, let's see how you do.
cues.zh: 于是国防部说，明年再来吧，看看你们表现如何。

cues.en: And so we did.
cues.zh: 于是我们照做了。

cues.en: Came back next year.
cues.zh: 第二年又回来了。

cues.en: For those of you who aren't familiar, the black part is supposed to be down.
cues.zh: 可能有人不太清楚，黑色的部分本来应该朝下的。

cues.en: Again, 10 days before the race, we got it put together.
cues.zh: 同样，在比赛前10天，我们才把它组装好。

cues.en: But we weren't the only people having fun out in the desert.
cues.zh: 不过在沙漠里找乐子的可不止我们。

cues.en: These good folks from Stanford took their vehicles out and had some entertaining times.
cues.zh: 来自 Stanford 的这群好朋友把他们的车开出来，也度过了一些有趣的时光。

cues.en: And then these poor folks from Berkeley somehow found a lake.
cues.zh: 然后伯克利这帮可怜的家伙不知怎么就开进湖里了。

cues.en: And this was truly tragic because the next day they had an interview with the New York Times.
cues.zh: 这真是太惨了，因为第二天他们还要接受《纽约时报》的采访。

cues.en: And what was amazing was they took this thing out, dumped the water out of it, fixed it up,
cues.zh: 但神奇的是，他们把车捞了出来，排掉里面的水，修好了它，

cues.en: and the next day ran a demo for the New York Times.
cues.zh: 第二天还真给《纽约时报》做了现场演示。

cues.en: So really, the spirit of innovation and effort was really there.
cues.zh: 所以说，那种创新和拼搏的精神确实是在那里的。

cues.en: At the end of this challenge, five vehicles actually completed this 150-mile race.
cues.zh: 在那次挑战赛的最后，实际上有五辆车完成了这整整 150 英里的赛程。

cues.en: This was the vehicle from Stanford that won the competition, and it's now housed in the Smithsonian.
cues.zh: 这就是斯坦福赢得比赛的那辆车，现在它被收藏在史密森尼学会博物馆里。

cues.en: And we were able to get up on our soap boxes and say, holy cow, these robot cars,
cues.zh: 我们也终于可以站在台上大声宣称：天哪，这些自动驾驶汽车，

cues.en: they're going to do something good for the world.
cues.zh: 它们真能为这个世界做出一番贡献。

cues.en: But we didn't know yet whether we could actually make it work.
cues.zh: 但当时我们其实还不确定，到底能不能真的把它做成功。

cues.en: And the Defense Department said, that's great.
cues.zh: 国防部说，太棒了。

cues.en: You know, you drove across the desert.
cues.zh: 你看，你们穿过了沙漠。

cues.en: You didn't bump into too many things.
cues.zh: 也没撞上太多东西。

cues.en: Why don't we have you come to an air base and drive around there and see how you do
cues.zh: 不如你们来空军基地开一圈，看看表现如何，

cues.en: with traffic?
cues.zh: 在有交通流的情况下？

cues.en: And so they came up with the urban challenge.
cues.zh: 于是他们推出了城市挑战赛（Urban Challenge）。

cues.en: And the idea here was we put robots at the Subbanan air base.
cues.zh: 这想法就是把机器人放在空军基地里。

cues.en: They had to stay on their side of the road now.
cues.zh: 这次它们必须在自己的车道行驶了。

cues.en: They had to navigate stop sign intersections, and they had to deal with other vehicles,
cues.zh: 得通过有停步标志的路口，还得应对其他车辆，

cues.en: both robotic, the ones with all the stuff on the top, and human-driven, you know, paid
cues.zh: 既有机器人车辆——就是顶上装满设备的那些，也有人类驾驶的——也就是雇来的

cues.en: stunt drivers that were out there.
cues.zh: 特技车手。

cues.en: there to create traffic for the cars to interact with.
cues.zh: 他们在那儿制造车流，供自动驾驶汽车交互。

cues.en: And the vehicles had to drive 60 miles that day.
cues.zh: 那天车辆必须行驶 60 英里。

cues.en: And they had to do it again without any help.
cues.zh: 而且全程依然不能有人类协助。

cues.en: And at the end of the day, we had two crashes.
cues.zh: 到头来，我们还是出了两起车祸。

cues.en: First reported robot on robot car crash, so big day.
cues.zh: 这是有记录以来第一次机器人撞上机器人，真是个“大日子”。

cues.en: But also, we had six vehicles that finished that challenge.
cues.zh: 但同时，我们也有六辆车跑完了全程。

cues.en: And this was something that just four years before,
cues.zh: 而就在四年前，

cues.en: everyone said was basically impossible.
cues.zh: 大家都还觉得这基本是不可能的。

cues.en: And so in 2007 we were really excited about the progress and the Defense Department said
cues.zh: 所以在 2007 年，我们为这一进展感到非常兴奋，国防部也说，

cues.en: that's fantastic, you guys have made such progress, problem is solved.
cues.zh: 太棒了，你们取得了这么大的进展，问题解决了。

cues.en: Someone now should pick this up and figure out how to turn it into a product.
cues.zh: 现在该有人接手，去想想怎么把它做成产品了。

cues.en: And so this huge community that had gathered together to go after these challenges and
cues.zh: 于是，曾经汇聚起来共同应对挑战、

cues.en: compete and cooperate said, you know, basically dwindled and diminished into nothing.
cues.zh: 相互竞争又合作的庞大群体，基本就逐渐瓦解、烟消云散了。

cues.en: But in 2000, oh, sorry, people want it.
cues.zh: 但在 2000 年，噢抱歉，大家想要这个。

cues.en: In 2009, Google said, let's actually do something about this.
cues.zh: 到了 2009 年，Google 决定：我们来真真正正做点什么吧。

cues.en: Let's see if this technology really
cues.zh: 让我们来看看这项技术是否真的

cues.en: is ready to go out into the field and have people use it.
cues.zh: 准备好走向大众、投入实用了。

cues.en: This is when I came to Google and we founded the team.
cues.zh: 就在那时，我来到了 Google，我们组建了团队。

cues.en: And the mission of that team was to improve people's lives
cues.zh: 这个团队的使命就是

cues.en: by transforming mobility.
cues.zh: 通过革新出行方式来改善人们的生活。

cues.en: And what does that really mean?
cues.zh: 那这究竟意味着什么呢？

cues.en: Well, first and foremost, it's about safety.
cues.zh: 首先，最重要的就是安全。

cues.en: So on America's roads, we kill 38,000 people every year.
cues.zh: 在全美的道路上，每年有 3.8 万人丧生。

cues.en: To put that in perspective, that's more than a 737 falling out of the sky five days a week.
cues.zh: 换个角度来说，这相当于每周有五天、每天都有一架 737 客机坠毁。

cues.en: Now we completely wouldn't accept that in aviation, so why do we accept it on our roads?
cues.zh: 我们绝不会容忍航空业发生这种事，那为什么能在道路上接受呢？

cues.en: And those numbers, though harrowing, really, aren't telling the whole story.
cues.zh: 而这些数据虽然触目惊心，却还不是全部的真相。

cues.en: So we've driven 1.4 million miles, and our car's seen a lot of things, like people parked
cues.zh: 我们已经行驶了 140 万英里，车子目睹了各种状况，比如有人把车停在

cues.en: in bushes.
cues.zh: 灌木丛里。

cues.en: If you look on the left here, somebody parked in the median.
cues.zh: 看看左边这里，有人把车停在了中间隔离带上。

cues.en: We've had cars make left-turn U-turns from the middle of the road.
cues.zh: 我们遇到过有车直接在马路中间左转掉头。

cues.en: We've had motorcycles, if you watch closely in the bottom left here, sneak past us, taking
cues.zh: 要是你仔细看左下角，会看到有摩托车从我们身边挤过去，

cues.en: life in their hands.
cues.zh: 简直是在拿生命开玩笑。

cues.en: And watch this bicyclist attempt to run a red light, and then just at the last moment,
cues.zh: 再看这个骑自行车的人，本想闯红灯，但就在最后一刻，

cues.en: think better of it and get out of the way.
cues.zh: 他打消了念头，让开了路。

cues.en: We've had people stopped at red lights, and then for no real good reason, just charge
cues.zh: 我们还碰到过有人在红灯前停下，接着却莫名其妙地，

cues.en: off through them.
cues.zh: 直接冲了过去。

cues.en: And we've had people, as we're making turns with the light, decide, you know, whatever,
cues.zh: 还有当我们顺着信号灯转弯时，有人却觉得“不管了，

cues.en: I'm going to go.
cues.zh: 我就要走”。

cues.en: And our cars have to deal with that and react to it.
cues.zh: 而我们的车必须去应对并做出反应。

cues.en: And we've seen worse.
cues.zh: 我们还见过更糟糕的情况。

cues.en: So watch in the bottom left as two motorcycles pass us, and then a truck hits them.
cues.zh: 请看左下角，两辆摩托车从我们身边超过去，然后一辆卡车撞上了他们。

cues.en: Everybody walked away.
cues.zh: 大家都安然无恙地离开了。

cues.en: And then here, watch these two cars join in the intersection.
cues.zh: 再看这里，这两辆车在十字路口汇合。

cues.en: And so over the 1.4 million miles that we've driven, we're now even more confident that
cues.zh: 在我们行驶的 140 万英里中，我们现在更加确信，

cues.en: this technology can't get out into the world soon enough, just from the safety benefits
cues.zh: 这项技术越早普及越好，单从安全层面的

cues.en: alone. And it's not just about safety. So it turns out people sell cars like this.
cues.zh: 益处来说就是如此。而且这不仅仅关乎安全。事实证明，人们是这样卖车的。

cues.en: And as you know, this is what we get. Turns out between 1990 and 2010, we drove 38 percent
cues.zh: 但如你所知，我们实际得到的是这样。数据显示在 1990 到 2010 年间，全美的行车里程

cues.en: more miles in this country. But we only added 6 percent more lanes. So that traffic really
cues.zh: 增加了 38%。但我们仅增加了 6% 的车道。所以交通

cues.en: is getting worse. It's not your parents just telling you a story about when they
cues.zh: 确实在恶化。这可不是父母在跟你讲他们年轻时的

cues.en: young. Traffic sucks and it's getting worse. And it has a real cost. So if you take the
cues.zh: 陈年旧事。堵车糟透了，而且越来越严重。它带来了实打实的代价。如果把全美的

cues.en: average commute in America, you multiply it by the number of workers, you get to six billion
cues.zh: 平均通勤时间乘以工作人口总数，你会发现人们每天堵在路上的时间

cues.en: minutes per day of people sat in traffic. You take that and divide it by the average
cues.zh: 高达 60 亿分钟。如果再除以美国人的

cues.en: American lifetime of 70 years. That's 162 wasted lifetimes per day of people sitting
cues.zh: 平均寿命 70 年，相当于每天因为堵车

cues.en: in traffic. Try and contemplate that for a moment. It's incredible. We're literally
cues.zh: 白白浪费了 162 个人的一生。试着想一想这个数字。简直令人难以置信。我们真的

cues.en: killing people with gridlock.
cues.zh: 是在用交通拥堵来谋杀生命。

cues.en: And then there's those people who don't have that privilege of sitting in traffic.
cues.zh: 还有那些甚至连堵在路上的特权都没有的人。

cues.en: So this is Steve.
cues.zh: 这位是 Steve。

cues.en: You know, he's an incredible guy.
cues.zh: 他是一个非常了不起的人。

cues.en: It turns out for him, instead of taking 30 minutes to get to work in the morning, it
cues.zh: 事实对他而言，早上上班原本只要30分钟的路程，

cues.en: takes two hours because he's blind.
cues.zh: 却要花上两个小时，因为他双目失明。

cues.en: And he has to patch together various kinds of public transit or ask friends and family.
cues.zh: 他不得不辗转搭乘各种公共交通，或者向亲友求助。

cues.en: And so for someone like Steve, who used to be able to drive and has lost that privilege,
cues.zh: 所以对于像 Steve 这样曾经能开车、如今却失去这一权利的人来说，

cues.en: his world changes.
cues.zh: 他的世界彻底变了。

cues.en: And we can give people like that back their mobility and let them engage properly with
cues.zh: 而我们可以让这样的人重获出行能力，让他们真正融入

cues.en: life.
cues.zh: 生活。

cues.en: And so when I say we're about improving people's lives by transforming mobility, it's that
cues.zh: 因此，当我提到我们要通过变革出行方式来改善人们的生活时，

cues.en: whole spectrum of issues that we'd like to kind of address with the technology.
cues.zh: 我们希望用技术解决的，正是这一整套层面的问题。

cues.en: Our program can really be broken down into three phases.
cues.zh: 我们的项目实际上可以分为三个阶段。
